did: I was the first worker on making the Rust essay show the phone's own screens. The reach (call C790) chose to fold existing tools in rather than build: home's essay recorder now photographs each ticket's card exactly as the phone draws it, from the owner's real week, with the question, each speak-to point, the program, rustc's result and each diagnostic named and boxed, so a later scene can zoom to any of them. The record of screens and regions is generic, so the public showcase essay can capture other screens the same way. Nothing leaves home: the page refuses every request but the stage's own and the week's file.

calls.title: How the essay's phone pictures are captured (C790)
options: Photograph the phone's own card with Playwright inside home's essay recorder, and zoom with HyperFrames
Use Snips Capture as it is, on GitHub's runners
Wait for the emulator walk driver (WALK1)
Render the code with a third-party code renderer
calls.why: The picture has to be the owner's real week as their phone draws it, and that week may not leave home. Snips Capture runs on GitHub with sample data and names no parts, WALK1 isn't built, and a code renderer draws its own theme, not the phone's.
calls.undo: Remove the --week-file capture from record:essay and the /rust-screen stage; the essay goes back to its text cards.

left: Nothing is captured on home until server#1049 lands and home's render image includes this change: home must hand the recorder the week with its rustc runs.
The zoom itself is W2's: one HyperFrames composition both essays can place as a composition scene.
A deep dive's own code snippet isn't on the phone, so those dives stay text cards for now; noted on #3288.
A speak-to point's box leaves out its list number, 20 px to its left, so the zoom pads its target.
